questions.question: Who has the power to recommend for the imposition of Constitutional Emergency in a state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Governor of the state.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Governor of the state** has the power to **recommend** for the **imposition of Constitutional Emergency in a state.**
 
• A **Constitutional Emergency or President's Rule or State Emergency** can be **imposed by the President under Article 356** of the Indian Constitution when the Governor of a state believes that the state cannot be governed according to the Constitution.
 
• The Governor can recommend the imposition of a Constitutional Emergency to the President of India. If the President is satisfied that a Constitutional Emergency is necessary, he can issue a proclamation imposing the same.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 352 to 360 in Part XVIII** of the Constitution of India deals with the **emergency provisions**.
 
• There are **three types of emergencies** specified by the Constitution.
 
 
• **National Emergency:** Under **Article 352**, the president can declare a **national emergency** when the security of India or a part of it is threatened **by war or external aggression or armed rebellion.**
 
• **President's Rule: Article 356** empowers the President to issue a proclamation if he is satisfied that a situation has arisen in which the government of a state cannot be carried on in accordance with the provisions of the constitution.
 
• **Financial Emergency: Article 360** empowers the president to proclaim a Financial Emergency if he is satisfied that a situation has arisen due to which the financial stability or credit of India or any part of its territory is threatened.

questions.question: In the state legislative assembly, the Money bill can be introduced with the prior permission of __________.

__
 
• The Governor is the head of a state in India.
 
• The Governor's role includes giving assent to bills passed by the state legislature.
 
• A Money Bill can only be introduced in the legislative assembly of a state with the prior permission of the Governor.
 
• The Governor has the authority to recommend the introduction of money bills in the state legislature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Money Bill**

 
 
• A Money Bill is defined in Article 110 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• It deals with issues related to taxation, borrowing of money by the government, expenditure from the state or central consolidated fund, and other financial matters.
 
• A Money Bill can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha (at the central level) or the Legislative Assembly (at the state level).
 
• The Rajya Sabha (at the central level) or the Legislative Council (at the state level) can only make recommendations on a Money Bill, which the Lok Sabha or Legislative Assembly may choose to accept or reject.
 
 
 
• **Role of the Governor**
 
 
• The Governor is appointed by the President of India for a term of five years.
 
• The Governor acts as a representative of the President in the state.
 
• In addition to legislative duties, the Governor has executive and judicial functions.
 
• The Governor can grant pardons, reprieves, respites, or remissions of punishment or suspend, remit or commute the sentence of any person convicted of any offense.
 
 
 
• **Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG)**
 
 
• The CAG is an authority established by the Constitution of India under Article 148.
 
• The CAG audits all receipts and expenditure of the Government of India and the state governments, including those of bodies and authorities substantially financed by the government.
 
• The CAG reports are laid before the Parliament and state legislatures.
 
 
 
• **Finance Minister**
 
 
• The Finance Minister is a key position in the government responsible for managing the financial resources of the country or state.
 
• The Finance Minister presents the annual budget, oversees revenue collection, and manages public expenditure.
 
• The Finance Minister plays a crucial role in economic planning and development.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India deals with the 'Pardoning Power of the Governor'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 161.**__

__
 
• **Article 161** of the Indian constitution deals with the Pardoning Power of the Governor.

• Types of Pardoning Powers of the President -

 
 
• Pardon - It removes both the sentence and the conviction of the convict and completely absolves the convict from all sentences, punishments and disqualifications.
 
• Commutation - It substitutes one form of punishment for a lighter form. 
 
• Remission - It reduces the period of the sentence but the character of the sentence remains the same. 
 
• Respite - It denotes awarding a lesser sentence in place of one originally awarded due to some special fact such as the physical disability of a convict or the pregnancy of a woman offender, the President can use this power. 
 
• Reprieve - It implies a stay of the execution of a sentence (especially that of death) for a temporary period. Its purpose is to enable the convict to have time to seek pardon or commutation from the President.

questions.question: As per the Constitution of India, what is the maximum number of states for which the same person can be appointed as Governor?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**There is no limit.**__

__
 
• As per the Constitution of India,** there is no limit **in the number of states for which the same person can be appointed as Governor.
 
• When the same person is appointed as the governor of two or more states, **the emoluments and allowances payable to him are shared by the states in such proportion as determined by the president.**
 
• His emoluments and allowances cannot be diminished during his term of office.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

There shall be a Governor for each state.

The Governor of a state shall be appointed by the President of India on the recommendation of the Council of Ministers.

4) The Governor can reduce the amount of the sentence without changing its character (remission) For example A sentence of imprisonment for 2 years may be remitted to one year.

 5) The Governor can commute (substitute one form of punishment for another of a lighter character) for example:- rigorous imprisonment by simple imprisonment, simple imprisonment by fine, and so on.

questions.question: In India, the total number of members in the Legislative Council of a State having such a Council shall not exceed ___________ of the total number of members in the Legislative Assembly of that State.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**one-third**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The total number of members in the Legislative Council of a State in India shall not exceed **one-third** of the total number of members in the Legislative Assembly of that State.
 
• However, the total number of members in the Legislative Council should not be less than 40.
 
• The provision for the Legislative Council is given in Article 171 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Not all states in India have a Legislative Council; it exists only in a few states.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Legislative Council**

 
 
• Also known as Vidhan Parishad, it is the upper house in those states of India that have a bicameral legislature.
 
• Members of the Legislative Council are either elected by the Legislative Assembly, graduates, teachers, or are nominated by the Governor.
 
• The tenure of a member of the Legislative Council is 6 years, with one-third of the members retiring every 2 years.
 
• The presence of a Legislative Council helps in providing a revising chamber to the Legislative Assembly and acts as a check on hasty legislation.
 
 
 
• **Legislative Assembly**
 
 
• Also known as Vidhan Sabha, it is the lower house of the state legislature in India.
 
• Members of the Legislative Assembly are directly elected by the people of the state through general elections.
 
• The tenure of the Legislative Assembly is 5 years unless dissolved sooner.
 
• The Legislative Assembly is responsible for making laws on the state list and concurrent list subjects, as well as controlling the state's finances.

__
 
• **Governor**

 
 
• In India, the governor of a state holds office at the pleasure of the president, which means that the president can remove the governor from office at any time without assigning any reason.
 
• This power is vested in the president under Article 156(1) of the Constitution of India.
 
• The president is advised by the Council of Ministers, which is headed by the Prime Minister.
 
• In practice, this means that the decision to remove a governor is usually taken by the central government, led by the Prime Minister.
 
• There are a number of reasons why the central government might want to remove a governor. These could include:
 
• If the governor is acting in a way that is considered to be unconstitutional or illegal.
 
• If the governor is not fulfilling their constitutional duties, such as providing assents to bills passed by the state legislature.
 
• If the governor is not acting in accordance with the advice of the Council of Ministers.
 
• If the governor is acting in a way that is considered to be detrimental to the interests of the state or the country.
 
• However, the central government is unlikely to remove a governor without a clear and compelling reason. This is because removing a governor is a serious matter that can damage the relationship between the central government and the state government.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Deputy Speaker**

 
 
• The Deputy Speaker of Lok Sabha is the second-highest legislative officer of the Lok Sabha.
 
• Article 93 of the Constitution provides for the election of both the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker.
 
• The Lok Sabha has not had a Deputy Speaker for the last 16 months. Instead, a panel of MPs has been assisting the Speaker.
 
 
 
• **Chief Minister**
 
 
• Chief Minister is the real executive authority i.e., de facto executive.
 
• The Constitution does not contain any specific procedure for the selection and appointment of the Chief Minister.
 
• Article 164 only says that the Chief Minister shall be appointed by the governor.
 
• The governor has to appoint the leader of the majority party in the state legislative assembly as the Chief Minister.
 
• But, when no party has a clear majority in the assembly, then the governor may exercise his personal discretion and then ask him to prove the majority within a reasonable period.
 
 
 
• **Speaker**
 
 
• Article 93 deals with the appointment of the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker.
 
• The inaugural holder of the office of the Lok Sabha was M. A. Ayyangar.
 
• The term length of the deputy speaker of the Lok Sabha is five years during the term of the Lok Sabha.
